subject: Netpath SLO scoping & ops handoff
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Khan <julia.khan@orionanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: SLO targets and next steps for private deployment

Thanks again for the demo this morning. High level notes / asks to make sure we're aligned before we loop in our infra team for the hands-on tests: 

- Target latency: 95th percentile <= 120ms for 2k token average inference (streaming enabled).
- Concurrency: sustained 120 concurrent streaming sessions during peak windows; target burst tolerance to 200 for up to 5 minutes.
- Throughput / egress: baseline 6 Gbps sustained, with ability to burst to 12 Gbps for short windows.
- VPN/peering: we will peer to your VPC via site-to-site VPN initially; want to validate NAT traversal and MTU handling.
- Internal latency budget: we need per-hop guidance (our app -> VPN -> redwood edge -> GPU hosts) so we can allocate margin.

Please advise on: a) minimal packet-per-second requirements for streaming b) recommended jitter/MTU settings c) any telemetry we should enable on our side to capture accurate tail latency.

Attaching a quick network diagram and the snippets our network team can share. Happy to schedule a 30-minute ops handoff once you confirm the test plan.

Attachments: orion_net_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram), orion_vpn_config_snippets.txt (config snippets)

--
Samir Patel
Head of MLOps, Orion Analytics
samir.patel@orionanalytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Julia Khan <julia.khan@orionanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO targets and next steps for private deployment

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. High level confirmation from our side and proposed next steps: 

- Targets: 95p <= 120ms (streaming) and sustained 120 concurrent sessions is doable with the config you described; we'll validate in lab and during your preflight window.
- Burst tolerance: we'll exercise autoscaling + short-lived extra capacity during tests to validate behavior up to 200 concurrent sessions.
- Egress: Redwood can support the 6 Gbps baseline; we'll verify sustained throughput during the POC and test bursts to 12 Gbps.

Proposed ops handoff plan (30–45m):
1) Karthik + Ben will own the network test plan and provide a checklist for your infra team.
2) We will run a latency/throughput sweep from our edge to your VPN endpoint and share packet captures + histogram outputs.
3) If we observe MTU or fragmentation issues, we'll recommend fixes and re-test.

Karthik / Ben — can you own the detailed checklist and propose two 1-hour windows for the POC next week?

I'll prepare an SLA proposal draft for your legal/ops review (attaching a starting doc).

Thanks,
--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Julia Khan <julia.khan@orionanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 2 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO targets and next steps for private deployment

On Wed, May 1, 2028 at 4:04 PM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Karthik / Ben — can you own the detailed checklist and propose two 1-hour windows for the POC next week?

Yep — we'll own this. Draft test plan below; please confirm and we'll convert to a runbook (JIRA-OPS-1247):

POC network test plan (summary):
- Preflight (ours and yours): exchange IP ranges, pre-provision firewall rules, and confirm VPN phase2 params.
- MTU & fragmentation check: send increasing MTU pings (1472, 1400, 1300) and confirm path MTU.
- Baseline latency sweep: 1k serial streaming requests (50–2k tokens) to establish median/95/99.
- Concurrency ramp: ramp from 20 -> 50 -> 100 -> 150 -> 200 concurrent streams (5 minute holds). Capture token-level latencies and KV cache hit rates.
- Egress throughput: synthetic traffic to measure sustained and burst throughput (measure with iperf and our tokenized payload simulator).
- Telemetry: enable pcap + flow logs on your VPN endpoint and our edge; we'll also request app-level timing headers.

Minimal instrumentation we need from your end:
- syslog of VPN tunnel drops and phase changes
- SNMP or sFlow counters for interface utilization (1s granularity if possible)
- PCAP capture window during the concurrency ramp

Two proposed windows (PDT):
- Option A: Tue 9 May 2028, 10:00–11:00
- Option B: Wed 10 May 2028, 14:00–15:00

If either works, we'll create the JIRA runbook and a shared Drive folder for artifacts. Also attaching a short checklist file for your network team to paste into their change window.

- Karthik

Attachments referenced: redwood_sla_proposal_20280501.pdf
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Khan <julia.khan@orionanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO targets and next steps for private deployment

Thanks — Option B works best for us (Wed 10 May 14:00 PDT). We'll provision a test VPN peer, enable PCAP during the window, and share SNMP counters. Julia from our side will lead the packet captures.

A few clarifications before the run: 
- Can Redwood provide a small client-side script to hit streaming endpoints with token-sized payloads? If not, we'll adapt your simulator.
- For the concurrency ramps, do you prefer gradual ramp (10% steps every 2 minutes) or stepped holds as proposed? Stepped holds are fine, but we want to make sure our autoscaling is triggered reliably.

I'll upload the final network diagram and the VPN config snippet to the shared Drive link and create an Ops ticket with our change window.

Attachments uploaded: orion_net_diagram_v2.pdf (updated)

--
Samir
